annotations.description: Jack-o'-Lantern is actually the best card to discard here for this deck's strategy. The Poxwalkers return from the graveyard whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand, so discarding a Poxwalkers would effectively not lose a card - it would set up the recursive engine. The reasoning given was completely wrong (calling Jack-o'-Lantern a '1/1 creature' when it's an artifact), but the actual choice of discarding Jack-o'-Lantern over Poxwalkers is a minor missed opportunity. Discarding a Poxwalkers would put it in the graveyard ready to be recurred, while Jack-o'-Lantern can at least be exiled from the graveyard for mana. However, the Poxwalkers synergy with the self-mill/combo plan makes discarding one of them clearly better.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Poxwalkers, which can return from the graveyard to the battlefield when spells are cast from non-hand zones, effectively making it free to discard and setting up the recursive engine.

annotations.description: Playing Verdant Catacombs before casting Once Upon a Time. If Once Upon a Time is still the first spell (free cast), it should be cast first to gain information before committing to a land drop. The top 5 cards might reveal a better land or change which creature to prioritize, affecting whether/how to use the fetchland.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Verdant Catacombs before casting Once Upon a Time
annotations.betterLine: Cast Once Upon a Time first (for free if first spell), see what creature or land is available, then make an informed decision about which land to play and whether to fetch.

annotations.description: Discarded Cabal Ritual instead of Poxwalkers. Poxwalkers has a recursion ability that triggers when casting spells from non-hand zones, meaning it's actually better in the graveyard for the Oops All Spells combo plan. Additionally, Cabal Ritual provides valuable mana acceleration redundancy for casting Balustrade Spy or Undercity Informer.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Cabal Ritual to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard Poxwalkers, which benefits from being in the graveyard (returns to battlefield when casting spells from anywhere other than hand) while preserving mana acceleration redundancy for the combo turn

annotations.description: Cast Once Upon a Time before activating Verdant Catacombs. Fetching first would thin a land from the library, slightly improving the quality of the top 5 cards seen by Once Upon a Time. Activating a fetchland is not casting a spell, so Once Upon a Time would still be free afterward.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Once Upon a Time before activating Verdant Catacombs
annotations.betterLine: Activate Verdant Catacombs first to fetch a Forest (thinning the deck), then cast the free Once Upon a Time to see better top-5 cards, then deploy a mana dork with the fetched land.

annotations.description: With only Verdant Catacombs as their sole land, taking Wight of the Reliquary over Misty Rainforest risks missing land drops. While they have two mana dorks in hand, they can only deploy one per turn, and if the dork gets removed they'd be stuck on one land. A fetchland would guarantee consistent mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Wight of the Reliquary from Once Upon a Time
annotations.betterLine: Take Misty Rainforest to ensure a second land drop. With Birds of Paradise and Ignoble Hierarch already in hand for mana development, securing consistent land drops is more important than adding another creature to a hand already full of plays.

annotations.description: With only one Bayou available producing either B or G, casting Ignoble Hierarch (which produces B, R, or G but not the blue needed for anything) is reasonable for mana acceleration, but Thoughtseize might be more impactful here. The opponent has been casting Dark Rituals and Cabal Rituals, suggesting a combo deck. Thoughtseize would strip a key combo piece from their hand before they can go off, while Ignoble Hierarch just adds a mana dork that may not survive to be useful if the opponent combos next turn. However, Ignoble Hierarch does enable casting multiple spells next turn (like Thoughtseize + a 2-drop), so there's a reasonable argument for the mana dork line.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ignoble Hierarch to develop mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thoughtseize to strip a combo piece from the opponent's hand, since the opponent appears to be on a fast combo deck (Dark Ritual, Cabal Ritual, Undercity Informer) that could go off before the mana dork provides value. The extra mana next turn matters less if the opponent kills you on their turn 3.

annotations.description: Exiling Cabal Ritual to pay for Unmask breaks the combo line of Dark Ritual → Cabal Ritual → Balustrade Spy (which would generate exactly 4 black mana needed for Spy). Without Cabal Ritual, Dark Ritual alone only produces 3 mana, which is insufficient for either combo creature to function (Balustrade Spy costs 4, Undercity Informer costs 3 but needs a creature + 1 mana to activate).
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Cabal Ritual to pay for Unmask's alternative cost
annotations.betterLine: Exile one of the two Poxwalkers instead. Poxwalkers naturally return from the graveyard when spells are cast from non-hand zones (like flashback Cabal Therapy), and having two copies makes one expendable. This preserves the critical Dark Ritual → Cabal Ritual → Balustrade Spy combo line.

annotations.description: With Bayou and Ignoble Hierarch available (producing BG and B/R/G respectively), Libby has access to BG mana, which is exactly what Wight of the Reliquary costs. Wight is a 2/2 with vigilance that grows with creatures in the graveyard (currently 4 creature cards: Ignoble Hierarch, Grist the Hunger Tide which counts as a creature in graveyard, and potentially others depending on exact graveyard contents). With 4 creatures in graveyard (Ignoble Hierarch, Grist), Wight would be at least a 4/4. Additionally, Wight can sacrifice creatures to tutor lands, providing both board presence and utility. Birds of Paradise is a 0/1 mana dork that adds one mana of any color - useful but much less impactful than a large threat. Alternatively, Badgermole Cub costs 1G and provides a 2/2 body plus earthbend (animating a land as a creature with a +1/+1 counter) plus the mana-doubling ability with Ignoble Hierarch. However, Wight of the Reliquary is likely the strongest play here as it puts significant pressure on the board immediately as a large creature. Playing Birds of Paradise when you could deploy a meaningful threat is a tempo loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Birds of Paradise (0/1 mana dork) for G
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first (to have more mana available), then cast Wight of the Reliquary for BG using Bayou and Ignoble Hierarch, deploying a large threat (at least 4/4 with vigilance given creatures in graveyard). Alternatively, cast Thoughtseize first to check opponent's hand before committing to a threat.

annotations.description: With 3 mana available (Forest, Ignoble Hierarch, Birds of Paradise), the player could cast both Thoughtseize (B) and Wight of the Reliquary (BG) this turn. Leading with Thoughtseize first is better sequencing - it reveals the opponent's hand, strips their best card, and provides information before committing to a threat. Casting Wight first means if the opponent has removal, you've lost information about whether to play differently.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wight of the Reliquary before Thoughtseize
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thoughtseize first to gain information and strip the opponent's best card, then cast Wight of the Reliquary with remaining mana

annotations.description: Responding to Thoughtseize by casting Once Upon a Time gives the opponent more information and potentially a better card to take. The opponent sees whatever you find and can choose the best card from an expanded hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Once Upon a Time in response to Thoughtseize
annotations.betterLine: Let Thoughtseize resolve without responding. The opponent would choose from Once Upon a Time, Badgermole Cub, and Wight of the Reliquary - losing Once Upon a Time or Badgermole Cub is acceptable.

annotations.description: Balustrade Spy is the more dangerous combo piece - it mills the entire library on ETB for just {3}{B}, achievable with Dark Ritual + Elvish Spirit Guide. Undercity Informer requires both casting AND a separate activation with a creature sacrifice plus additional mana, making it harder to deploy in one turn. Taking Undercity Informer leaves the easier and more self-contained combo piece in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Name Balustrade Spy, as it's the more efficient and self-contained combo piece that can be cast immediately with the opponent's available mana sources (Dark Ritual + Elvish Spirit Guide).

annotations.description: Once Upon a Time costs {1}{G} when it's not the first spell of the game, and Kimi25 Libby has already cast multiple spells this game (Thoughtseize, Once Upon a Time previously, etc.). The 'cast without paying its mana cost' text says the annotation claims it was cast for free, but this is not the first spell of the game. If the game engine allowed this incorrectly, it's an engine issue. However, more importantly, casting Once Upon a Time before deploying creatures is questionable sequencing - Badgermole Cub would generate value by earthbending a land into a creature, and Wight of the Reliquary is already on board. With Bayou and Forest tapped and only Ignoble Hierarch and Birds of Paradise untapped for mana, spending {1}{G} on Once Upon a Time (if paid correctly) would consume the available mana that could cast Badgermole Cub instead. Badgermole Cub creates board presence and its earthbend ability makes a land into a creature (feeding Wight of the Reliquary's sacrifice ability). Additionally, Badgermole Cub's 'whenever you tap a creature for mana, add an additional {G}' would provide extra mana going forward. The Once Upon a Time is a speculative cantrip while Badgermole Cub develops the board meaningfully.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Once Upon a Time, apparently without paying its mana cost (which should not be free since it's not the first spell of the game).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Badgermole Cub using Ignoble Hierarch and Birds of Paradise for {1}{G}, getting the earthbend trigger and the mana-doubling ability for future turns. Then use Once Upon a Time later if mana permits.

annotations.description: Narcomoeba is a key combo piece in this Balustrade Spy/mill-your-library strategy - when milled from library to graveyard, it comes into play for free, providing a body for Cabal Therapy flashback or other sacrifice effects. Discarding it to the graveyard removes it from the library where it would auto-trigger. Meanwhile, Poxwalkers actively wants to be in the graveyard since it returns to the battlefield whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand (which the combo involves).
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Narcomoeba, removing it from the library where it would auto-trigger during the combo.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Poxwalkers, which benefits from being in the graveyard (auto-returns when casting spells from non-hand zones) and keeps Narcomoeba in library for the Balustrade Spy mill combo.

annotations.description: Missed lethal damage. By playing Gaea's Cradle before combat, then casting Badgermole Cub (earthbending a land into a 1/1 haste creature) and second Wight of the Reliquary, all creatures could attack for 11 damage against opponent's empty board at 10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Wight of the Reliquary (5 damage with exalted)
annotations.betterLine: Play Gaea's Cradle, tap it for 3G (3 creatures), tap Forest and Bayou for G+B, cast Badgermole Cub (earthbend a land), cast second Wight of the Reliquary, then attack with all creatures for 11+ damage (lethal against 10 life with empty board).

annotations.description: Discarded Elvish Spirit Guide instead of Poxwalkers. Poxwalkers has 'Curse of the Walking Pox' - it returns from graveyard to battlefield whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand (e.g., Cabal Therapy flashback). Discarding Poxwalkers to graveyard would set up a free creature, which enables sacrifice fodder for Undercity Informer or Cabal Therapy flashback. ESG at least provides a mana of any color that could supplement a combo turn.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Poxwalkers to put it in the graveyard where it can return to the battlefield for free when casting Cabal Therapy from graveyard, providing sacrifice fodder for the combo.
